summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease, and a history of bilateral lower extremity amputations was admitted for hyperkalemia and worsening kidney function, with a creatinine of 12.3 and potassium of 6.6. She was treated acutely with insulin, calcium, and sodium polystyrene sulfonate. Admission was complicated by accidental arterial puncture during left internal jugular central line placement, resulting in a hematocrit drop from 27.3 to 22.3, requiring transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells and suturing. A tunneled dialysis catheter was placed on hospital day two, and hemodialysis was initiated, leading to improvement in renal parameters. She was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae, sensitive to ciprofloxacin, and was treated with a short course of antibiotics. The patient was discharged home with services to begin outpatient dialysis, with follow-up planned for fistula creation and continued management of chronic conditions including diabetes, systolic heart failure, and anemia.
